Who is Understory?

Understory is a vertical-focused software platform built for experience businesses – from kayaking tours to cooking classes. Our operating system helps creators manage operations, grow bookings, accept payments, and run their business with clarity and less stress.

We move fast, iterate quickly, and expect everyone to bring proactive solutions every day. You'll learn faster here than almost anywhere else because the challenges are real and the pace is high. This isn't about clocking in and out – the right candidate will get a lot of trust and ownership, and it's all about building something that matters to creators around the world.

We recently raised a €12M Series A and are scaling fast. With customers in 10+ countries and a growing presence internationally, our focus is global, our ambition is high, and our team is fully committed to being the go-to platform for experience creators worldwide.

In keeping with this momentum, we are growing our team across Copenhagen and Barcelona and doubling down on our Nordic markets.

About the Role

As our Nordic Account Executive, you'll be responsible for driving revenue growth in our Nordic markets from our Copenhagen or Barcelona office. You'll own the sales process from qualified opportunity to signed customer, helping experience providers discover how Understory can support and grow their businesses.

You'll work closely with SDRs, Customer Success, and Marketing teams to create a seamless customer journey while providing valuable market insights that help shape our growth strategy in the Nordics.

What You'll Do

• 
Own the full back end of the sales cycle for Danish, Swedish or Norwegian experience providers.

• 
Conduct product demonstrations and consultative sales conversations.

• 
Convert qualified leads into paying customers through effective negotiation and closing.

• 
Collaborate with SDRs to ensure smooth transitions from prospecting to opportunity management.

• 
Maintain accurate pipeline data and forecasting in CRM systems.

• 
Share insights from the Nordic markets to support product and commercial strategy.

• 
Represent Understory at relevant events and networking opportunities.

What Success Looks Like

Months 1–3 - Onboarding & Pipeline: Complete onboarding, build pipeline ownership, and confidently manage sales conversations.

Months 4–6 - Closing: Consistently close new customers and establish a healthy sales pipeline.

Months 7–12 - Revenue: Achieve or exceed revenue targets while contributing to Understory's long-term growth in the Nordics.

What We're Looking For

• 
You need to be native in one of our Nordic markets: native level of Danish, Swedish or Norwegian, plus fluency in English (written and spoken).

• 
2+ years of B2B sales experience, either as a top-performing SDR/BDR or as an Account Executive.

• 
Strong negotiation, presentation, and closing skills.

• 
A proactive and results-driven mindset with a passion for achieving goals.

• 
Passion for experiences, travel, and supporting entrepreneurs.

• 
Someone living in either Copenhagen or Barcelona to join one of our offices.

Nice to have:

• 
Experience within SaaS, hospitality, tourism, or experience-booking industries.

• 
Existing network within the Danish, Swedish or Norwegian tourism or events sector.

• 
Familiarity with CRM tools such as HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive.

• 
Experience working in a startup or scale-up environment.

• 
Additional European language capabilities.

Why You'll Thrive at Understory

• 
Be part of a high-growth company redefining the experience economy worldwide.

• 
Join Understory at a pivotal moment in our Nordic markets: as part of our growing Nordic team, you will help shape our regional strategy, local team culture, and market footprint.

• 
Work from our Copenhagen or Barcelona office while helping shape our growth in the Nordics.

• 
Enjoy autonomy, flexibility, and ownership in a fast-moving environment.

• 
Collaborate with ambitious colleagues who are passionate about building meaningful products.

• 
Benefit from significant opportunities for professional development and career progression.

Start Date & Application

If you're a high-achieving closer who is ready to take ownership of revenue growth and leave your mark as an Account Executive in the Nordics, we want to hear from you! Apply below to join us.

We review applications on a rolling basis and will hire as soon as we find the right person.

Factbird helps manufacturers improve performance with an AI-enabled, plug-and-play manufacturing intelligence suite. Real-time visibility on the shop floor. Connected operations. Data that actually turns into improvement, not just reports.

We’re expanding our Northern European sales team in Copenhagen and looking for a Business Development Representative to help us keep building momentum and opening doors in a market where we already have a solid presence. You’ll work from our Copenhagen office and support our Danish and Swedish markets, so we’re looking for someone fluent in both languages.

This is a great role for someone early in their sales career who wants more than a script to follow: someone who wants to help shape our outbound approach, sharpen their craft with modern prospecting tools, and sell something that makes a real difference on the factory floor.

About the Role

As a BDR at Factbird, you won’t just be executing outreach. You’ll be helping sharpen the playbook for how we generate pipeline in Denmark and Sweden. That means a mix of hands-on prospecting and real input into strategy: which accounts to target, which messages resonate, and which channels and tools actually move the needle.

You’ll spend your time identifying the right accounts, reaching the right people, testing what works, and turning interest into qualified meetings and sales opportunities.

This is a phone-first role. Phone calls remain your primary tool, but you’ll also run structured multi-channel campaigns across email and LinkedIn, and use AI-powered prospecting tools to work smarter, not just harder.

Key Responsibilities

We’re looking for someone who understands that outbound success comes from a combination of activity, discipline, messaging, and follow-through. This role is aligned with market expectations for outbound development work, including periods where 100-200 call attempts per day may be required, depending on territory focus, campaign goals, and lead quality.

What you'll do

• 
Build qualified pipeline through targeted outbound prospecting into manufacturing and industrial accounts across Denmark and Sweden

• 
Respond to inbound leads, qualify interest, and convert it into meetings

• 
Research target accounts to understand business context, likely pain points, and buying relevance

• 
Identify the right decision-makers and stakeholders within target organizations

• 
Book discovery meetings for the Account Management team and create qualified opportunities

• 
Maintain strong prospect data quality and keep HubSpot accurate and up to date

• 
Track your performance against KPIs and stay disciplined about activity and follow-up

• 
Work closely with the Account Management and Marketing teams to sharpen targeting, messaging, and handoff quality

• 
Bring insights from prospect conversations back to the team: what’s resonating, what isn’t

How we'll measure success

KPIs will be defined with your manager, but here's what we're tracking:

• 
Sales-qualified leads generated

• 
Discovery meetings booked and completed

• 
Conversion from leads to qualified opportunities

• 
Outreach volume, especially calls

• 
Inbound lead response time

• 
CRM discipline and data quality

This role is for someone who wants to see a direct line between their daily work, the strategies they help build, and commercial growth.

About you

You want to build a career in sales, and you’re ready for a role where you get real ownership, not just a list of calls to make. You’re comfortable in an outbound environment, curious about tools and experimentation, and motivated by the opportunity to improve fast. We’re looking for someone with:

• 
1-3 years of experience as an SDR in a B2B SaaS environment

• 
Fluency in Danish and Swedish, and strong English

• 
A strong interest in pipeline generation and outbound prospecting

• 
Comfort working in a phone-first sales development role

• 
The ability to succeed in a high-activity environment, including periods of 100-200 calls per day

• 
Curiosity about the manufacturing world and interest in learning how manufacturers operate

• 
Strong follow-through and personal ownership

• 
Experience working in a CRM, ideally HubSpot

• 
Hunger for a long-term career in sales

If you’re excited by building pipelines, learning fast, and helping bring modern software into manufacturing environments, we’d love to hear from you.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

• 
Flexible working hours — we trust you to manage your time

• 
Competitive salary — compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact

• 
Internet reimbursement — stay connected wherever you choose to work from

• 
Thoughtful, human onboarding — step-by-step support from day one

• 
Individual Development Plan conversations — bi-yearly career development aligned to your ambitions

• 
Company-wide kickoffs & team days — we come together regularly across teams and regions

• 
A global, inclusive culture — diverse backgrounds and perspectives, actively celebrated

Join Us

If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit, feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Please note that applications will be reviewed after November 20th.

At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws.

We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

For more information or questions please contact us at khma@factbird.com

**Business Consultant - AECO Technical Advisory

****Position Overview

**Autodesk Consulting is looking for a Business Consultant to join our Northern Europe team. This remote role supports strategic customers across the region.

This is a senior individual contributor role combining business consulting, AECO industry expertise and executive advisory. You’ll work with some of Autodesk’s largest customers to shape transformation strategies, define target operating models, and develop business cases and roadmaps that deliver measurable business outcomes.

You’ll advise senior leaders, structure complex business challenges and lead strategic advisory engagements from discovery through executive decision-making. While you won’t configure or implement solutions, you’ll understand how Autodesk and complementary technologies fit within customers’ broader business and technology ecosystems, partnering with technical specialists to turn strategy into actionable delivery plans.

**Main Responsibilities

**

• Build trusted relationships with customer executives, business leaders and transformation teams, acting as a strategic advisor throughout the engagement

• Understand customer objectives, challenges and operating context to define outcome-driven transformation strategies

• Assess operating models, business processes, organizational capabilities, data and digital workflows to identify opportunities for improvement

• Define target-state operating models, transformation roadmaps, business cases, success measures and benefits realization plans

• Lead executive workshops, facilitate decision-making and align stakeholders across complex organizations

• Advise customers on how Autodesk and complementary AECO technologies support business outcomes through effective workflows, data management and interoperability

• Identify and prioritize opportunities for data, automation and AI based on business value, organizational readiness, governance and adoption

• Partner with Solution Architects, technical consultants and customer-facing teams to shape advisory engagements, validate strategic recommendations and develop credible delivery roadmaps

**Minimum Qualifications

**

• Substantial experience in AECO, management consulting or business transformation, with a proven track record of independently leading complex strategy and transformation engagements

• Deep expertise in at least one of the following: construction, infrastructure, engineering consultancy, utilities, or a closely related project-based, asset-intensive industry

• Strong working knowledge of Autodesk technologies or comparable AECO tool ecosystems, with the ability to discuss capabilities, workflow fit, data, interoperability and business value. Hands-on implementation expertise is not required

• Strong understanding of operating models, organizational change, governance, business cases and benefits realization

• Practical understanding of data-centric workflows, enterprise systems, automation, responsible AI and technology adoption

• Ability to lead through influence across cross-functional and international teams, with excellent communication and executive presentation skills

• Fluent English is required. Dutch and other European languages are highly valued

• Willingness to travel to customer meetings and Autodesk events across Northern Europe (up to 50%)

• Proven experience advising executives, structuring complex problems, facilitating high-stakes workshops and driving decisions

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for an opportunity where you can make an impact, shape decisions, and accelerate your career?

**Be part of the movement - and play your part

**About The Role The DFDS Graduate Programme is a two-year fast-track programme for recent graduates with an interest in and passion for the maritime industry.

During the programme, you will complete three rotations across different areas of our Ferry Division. You will begin at our headquarters in Copenhagen, followed by a mandatory international rotation at one of our European hubs. Your final rotation at our headquarters will be tailored to your skills, interests, and our business needs.

Throughout the programme, you will gain broad exposure to both the operational and commercial sides of our Ferry Division while building valuable industry knowledge and professional experience.

Ferry Operations offers broad end-to-end exposure with sustainability, standardisation, and digitalisation at the heart of everything we do.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Help design and develop the vessels of tomorrow, supporting our green transition through electrification, ammonia, and green methanol initiatives.

• Support the operation and maintenance of our fleet of more than 70 RoRo, RoPax, and passenger vessels, covering everything from dry dock planning to crisis management and contingency handling.

• Contribute to our standardisation and digitalisation journey across eight owned terminals and more than 20 third-party terminals, where safety remains our highest priority.

• Support fleet planning, equipment optimisation, and our intercontinental rail setup, connecting ferry and logistics operations across our network.

In the commercial part of our Ferry Division, you will work alongside colleagues across Europe, supporting both B2B and B2C markets.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Support local and global sales teams and assist with key account management, ensuring our network is successfully marketed and sold across regions.

• Drive continuous improvement in customer service and booking processes through standardisation and digitalisation initiatives.

• Collaborate with IT teams to enhance and optimise our digital customer offerings.

• Work with operational teams to optimise routes and vessel capacity to meet customer demand.

• Support revenue management activities, including pricing optimisation and commercial performance analysis.

Across all rotations, you will work closely with highly skilled colleagues and engage with customers, suppliers, and partners throughout the maritime value chain. To support your development, each rotation will include both a dedicated manager and a mentor who will help you successfully navigate your learning journey.

Alongside hands-on experience at DFDS, you will participate in the Danish Shipping Education Programme, delivered by Danish Shipping. This programme consists of webinars, four seminars in Denmark, and one international seminar, covering key topics across the maritime industry.

• Have gained relevant experience through a student job, internship, exchange programme, or other extracurricular activities.

• Have no more than two years of full-time professional experience after completing your master's degree.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Are collaborative team players who enjoy working with others and creating impact.

• Are curious, proactive, and eager to learn and develop professionally.

• Have an international mindset and are excited about working across cultures and locations.

**JOB SUMMARY

**We are looking for an FP&A Specialist to strengthen our Corporate FP&A team and take ownership of cash flow forecasting, balance sheet planning, working capital management, and other key planning activities below Adjusted EBITDA across the Group.

Reporting directly to the Head of FP&A, you will play a key role in advancing our financial planning capabilities and driving transparency across cash flow, liquidity, and balance sheet performance. You will work closely with Accounting, Tax, Controlling, regional Finance teams, and key business stakeholders to ensure robust planning processes and high-quality management reporting.

This is a unique opportunity to:

• Take ownership of the Group's cash flow, balance sheet, and working capital planning agenda, helping to improve cash generation and support management decision-making.

• Shape and develop our Workday Adaptive Planning capabilities, leading key initiatives to establish scalable planning models and reporting structures.

• Work across markets and functions, partnering with regional Finance teams and senior stakeholders to strengthen forecasting, reporting, and business insight throughout the organization.

The successful candidate will help establish best-in-class planning processes that connect P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow forecasting, providing management with greater visibility into liquidity, working capital performance, and long-term value creation. The role is a full-time role and reports to the Head of Group Financial Planning & Analysis.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Own the Group's cash flow planning across forecast, budget, and long-range planning cycles.

• Drive the development of balance sheet forecasting capabilities and ensure alignment between P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow planning.

• Lead the implementation and continuous development of cash flow and balance sheet planning models in Workday Adaptive Planning.

• Define business requirements and partner closely with the BI Team to improve planning processes, reporting capabilities, and system functionality.

• Partner with Accounting, Controlling, Tax, and regional Finance teams to strengthen cash flow and balance sheet reporting, improve forecast accuracy, and establish clear ownership across planning activities.

• Develop and maintain monthly cash flow, balance sheet, and working capital reporting, including variance analysis, key risks and opportunities, and actionable management insights.

• Establish and maintain a clear RACI framework across Finance for balance sheet and cash flow planning, forecasting, and follow-up activities.

• Develop driver-based forecasting methodologies for key working capital metrics, including inventory, receivables, payables, and other material balance sheet accounts.

• Monitor working capital performance and identify opportunities to improve cash conversion and optimize working capital.

• Partner with Operations, Supply Chain, Accounting, and Controlling to strengthen understanding of working capital drivers and improve forecast accuracy.

• Support Executive Management and Board reporting by providing insights on cash generation, liquidity, working capital performance, and financial risks and opportunities.

• Drive continuous improvement of forecasting methodologies, planning processes, and financial transparency across the organization.

• Support the ongoing development of FP&A capabilities by integrating balance sheet and cash flow considerations into strategic and long-range planning processes.

**WHO YOU ARE

**You are a curious and analytical finance professional with a passion for turning data into insights and helping the business make better decisions. You enjoy working across functions, building strong stakeholder relationships, and taking ownership of complex planning processes.

You thrive in a dynamic and growing environment and are comfortable navigating between operational details and the bigger picture. You enjoy driving improvements, challenging assumptions, and creating structure where it is needed.

You are comfortable working across Finance functions and partnering with regional Finance teams to improve forecasting, strengthen financial transparency, and drive continuous improvement. Most importantly, you are proactive, structured, and motivated by creating impact through high-quality financial planning and analysis.

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING

**

• 5+ years of experience within FP&A, Financial Controlling, Corporate Finance, or a similar role.

• Strong understanding of financial statements, budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning.

• Experience working with cash flow forecasting, working capital, balance sheet analysis, or investment planning.

• Solid financial modelling and analytical skills, including advanced Excel capabilities.

• Experience with Workday Adaptive Planning or other EPM/planning tools is an advantage.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• A proactive mindset and a passion for improving processes, systems, and ways of working.

• Experience from retail, hospitality, food & beverage, consumer goods, or other multi-site businesses is considered a plus.

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

**Job Description Summary

**The Production Engineer – Project Engineer works hands-on with manufacturing and cross-functional teams to implement product and process changes for medical devices used in ultrasound, surgical visualization, and image-guided procedures.

The role supports manufacturing across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration and loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

This is a hands-on manufacturing engineering role, working directly with operators, technicians, engineers, and SMEs on the production floor to troubleshoot issues, execute trials and first builds, collect and evaluate data, implement process changes, and verify solutions in the actual manufacturing environment

The position combines practical manufacturing engineering with three core areas: ECO/NPI implementation and manufacturing readiness; NC, INV and CAPA activities and Equipment Qualification/Process Validation.

**Job Description

****This is an onsite opportunity at our manufacturing site in Herlev, Denmark.

****Roles & Responsibilities

**

• Lead ECO implementation, NPI, and manufacturing change activities from production impact assessment and cut-in strategy through implementation and closure.

• Coordinate first builds and production trials, including process updates, SOP/WI changes, training, data and evidence collection, and implementation reporting.

• Work hands-on with operators and technicians on the production floor to troubleshoot manufacturing issues, implement process changes, and verify solutions.

• Own and drive NC, INV, and CAPA activities (TrackWise), including investigations, root cause analysis, corrective actions, implementation, effectiveness checks, and closure.

• Facilitate root cause investigations and define corrective actions together with Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, and relevant SMEs.

• Lead and support Equipment Qualification and Process Validation, including risk assessments, validation planning, protocol execution, documentation, and reporting.

• Support URS, IQ/OQ/PQ, equipment qualification, test method validation, revalidation, and ongoing process review, as applicable.

• Develop and improve manufacturing processes using pFMEA, Control Plans, risk management, process controls, and continuous improvement.

• Ensure manufacturing changes, investigations, equipment, and processes are appropriately documented, controlled, validated, traceable, and audit-ready.

**Required Qualifications

**

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Experience with manufacturing engineering, ECO implementation, NPI, or sustaining engineering.

• Experience with NC, INV, CAPA, root cause analysis, and Quality System workflows.

• Experience with or strong understanding of Equipment Qualification and Process Validation.

• Knowledge of GMP, Quality Management Systems, risk management, and manufacturing process controls.

• Experience working in medical device or other regulated manufacturing environments.

• Proven ability to work cross-functionally across Engineering, Manufacturing, and Quality.

**Desired Characteristics (nice to have)

**

• Hands-on experience with medical device manufacturing and manufacturing process development/improvement.

• Strong project execution and manufacturing change implementation skills.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and root cause investigation capabilities.

• Experience with equipment qualification, process validation, and risk-based manufacturing activities.

• Structured and disciplined approach to documentation, workflows, actions, and deadlines.

• Proactive and solution-oriented with strong ownership and accountability.

• Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills.

• Ability to balance ECO/NPI, Quality System activities, validation, compliance, and production priorities

**Job Description

**_Transaction Banking is changing fast, and the way customers connect with their bank is becoming more sophisticated. Danske Bank is bringing its Customer Implementation and Integration areas together under one unit, and we are looking for a leader who can create a shared direction, build a strong leadership team, and make complex customer journeys simpler and more consistent across five markets.

_**What You Will Be Doing

**You will lead a newly unified organisation spanning Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland and Lithuania, bringing together experienced leaders, specialist teams and distinct capabilities. Reporting directly to the Head of TxB Sales Enablement, you will work closely with colleagues across Sales, Product, Technology, IT and Tribe organisations to shape end-to-end customer experiences. Your role sits at the intersection of business, operations and technology, and the decisions you make will shape how corporate customers and financial institutions connect with Danske Bank.

More specifically, you will:

• Set the strategic direction and priorities across all five markets

• Build and develop a leadership team grounded in clarity, empowerment and accountability

• Connect Customer Implementation and Integration to create more seamless customer journeys

• Partner with IT and Tribe teams to shape customer-facing solutions and internal tooling

• Use client insights to inform implementation journeys, integration solutions and commercial priorities

• Encourage the responsible adoption of AI to simplify processes and build employee capabilities

**About You

**

• Solid experience leading organisations through other leaders

jobs.occupation: Women’s Academy 2027: Insights into the financial sector
jobs.description:
Step inside the world of finance and explore what happens on a busy trading floor, how major companies are financed and how a bank manages risk in changing markets and society. Women’s Academy is an 8-week student programme at Danske Bank’s headquarters, designed to give you first-hand insight into Large Corporates & Institutions and Group Risk & Compliance.

What you will be doing

Across eight weekly sessions, you will meet specialists from across Danske Bank who will introduce you to their work, share real perspectives from the industry and involve you in relevant business topics.

During the programme, you will:

• 
Explore areas such as Corporate Banking, Markets, Corporate Finance, Risk and Compliance

• 
Gain insight into how different parts of Danske Bank work together

• 
Work with practical topics linked to finance, risk and business decisions

• 
Hear directly from people working in the financial sector

• 
Meet other students who are curious about finance

• 
Become part of the Women’s Academy community

• 
Take part in a celebratory dinner at the end of the programme

We welcome applications from university students between the second year of their bachelor’s degree and the second year of their master’s degree.

You do not need previous experience in banking or finance. You also do not need to know whether finance is the right career path for you yet. The Academy is a place to explore the sector from within and discover what captures your interest.

• 
Are curious about finance, business, markets or risk

• 
Want to learn more about career opportunities in the financial sector

• 
Are motivated to take an active part in discussions and sessions

• 
Bring an open mindset and a willingness to explore new topics

•

Location: Danske Bank headquarters, Copenhagen

The Human-Centred Computing Section, Department of Computer Science, invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in Human-Computer Interaction.

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project
 Digital technologies increasingly mediate how people experience, understand and respond to their bodies. The PhD project will investigate the relationship between bodies, technology and chronic illness, with a particular focus on self-tracking technologies. The project will explore how people with chronic conditions engage with these technologies and how technologies shape interactions with informal caregivers and health professionals. The project will critically examine how these technologies enact particular understandings of bodily difference and chronic illness, and how such understandings intersect with broader social, cultural and political norms. Within this topic, the PhD student will have some freedom to shape the focus of their work and the research questions they are interested in.

  The project will employ qualitative, participatory and design-oriented methods, with a particular emphasis on co-design and Research through Design. Co-design will involve working collaboratively with people with chronic conditions and other relevant stakeholders to explore their experiences of their bodies and technologies, and to imagine and develop new forms of technological interaction. Through Research through Design, the PhD researcher will develop and study experimental technological prototypes as a way of investigating alternative ways of sensing, representing and interacting with bodies. Design will be used not only to develop technological artefacts, but also as a means of generating knowledge about societal norms around chronic illness and the relationship between people and technology.

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of human-computer interaction (HCI). The ideal candidate should have a strong background in user-centred research methods, with some experience of working in a research environment. We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience in conducting design processes and developing both screen-based and physical computing prototypes. It is expected that candidates will have an M.Sc. degree in a relevant technical, design, or social science discipline. In addition, the ideal candidate will be able to document research capabilities (e.g., a thesis, publication, or project portfolio), have strong recommendations from supervisors and mentors, and possess a high level of intellectual humility. Preferred candidates would have advanced Danish language proficiency.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?
 The PhD fellow will become a member of the Human-Centered Computing (HCC) research section at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Computer Science. Here, we aim to fundamentally understand and improve the relation between computational technology and people. We are currently the top-ranked HCI research group in Europe (https://csrankings.org/#/index?chi&europe). Our research focuses on using computing to support people’s activities and well-being; inventing new ways for people to interact with technology, and understanding how human capabilities are influenced by technology. At the HCC section, we are currently over 15 faculty members, and over 20 postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, and research assistants. We hold joint weekly research meetings, many annual retreats, and have a thriving social environment from daily lunches to larger events. We attend the most important international conferences, such as CHI. We particularly value having a supportive and collegial work environment that values and encourages diversity. 

  Copenhagen is a vibrant city, with many cultural offerings and easy access to the rest of Europe. For more information about working in Denmark, consult International Staff Mobility.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Tariq Andersen, Department of Computer Science, tariq@di.ku.dk. The PhD project is led by Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, Department of Computer Science, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  The PhD programme 
 Depending of your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Computer Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 

  Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculy of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Computer Science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see:www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7,426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY FOR POSITION below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Research Statement (max. one page excl. references) detailing your desired research focus. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research project within the topic of designing self-tracking technologies for chronic conditions you would wish to explore. This should include specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature and, if relevant, your previous research, and the potential impact and applications of this research. As we are interested in your own ideas and writing style, please do not use generative AI. 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if relevant) 	
• Contact information for up to two people who have agreed to provide a reference.   Application deadline: 
 The deadline for applications is 29 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.
